## 🔄 Adapting Builds to Your Playstyle

These builds are starting points, not end states. Adjust based on:

**Your Skill Level**:
- New players → Balanced Combatant
- Intermediate → Bunker Tank or Team Anchor
- Advanced → Hypermobile Harasser or Solo God

**Your Typical Group Size**:
- Always solo → Solo God
- Duo/Trio → Team Anchor
- Full squad → Bunker Tank

**Content You Play**:
- Bunker runs → Bunker Tank
- Open world PvP → Hypermobile Harasser
- Farming/looting → Solo God
- Mixed → Balanced Combatant

---

## 📈 Build Tier List (January 2025)

**S-Tier (Must-Have)**:
1. Solo God - Best solo build by far
2. Bunker Tank - Essential for teams

**A-Tier (Excellent)**:
3. Hypermobile Harasser - High skill, high reward
4. Team Anchor - Underrated team value

**B-Tier (Good)**:
5. Balanced Combatant - Solid, flexible

**C-Tier (Niche)**:
- Pure crafting builds
- Experimental hybrid builds

---

## 💡 How to Copy These Builds

1. Use our [Skill Tree Builder](https://arcraiderskill.com/)
2. Import build codes (coming soon)
3. Allocate points in recommended order
4. Practice in safe environments first
5. Adjust based on your experience

---

## 🎓 Conclusion

The best build is the one that matches your playstyle and skill level. These meta builds are optimal for specific situations, but "optimal" doesn't mean "fun."

**Final Recommendation**:
- Try Balanced Combatant first
- Identify what you enjoy most
- Specialize into that role
- Master your chosen build

Meta changes, skills endure. Invest time in learning, not just copying.

# ARC Raiders Conditioning Guide | Stamina & Tank Builds

**URL:** https://arcraiderskill.com/blog/ultimate-conditioning-guide.html

Complete guide to the Conditioning skill branch in ARC Raiders. Learn how to maximize stamina efficiency, shield recovery, and survival sustainability for.

---

# ARC Raiders Conditioning Guide

2026-01-05 • 6 min read

The **Conditioning branch** in ARC Raiders skill tree is the cornerstone of tank-oriented builds focused on sustainability, shield efficiency, and prolonged combat effectiveness. This comprehensive guide will help you master every aspect of Conditioning.

## 🛡️ What is Conditioning?

Conditioning is one of the three main skill branches in ARC Raiders, centered around:
- **Stamina management** and regeneration
- **Shield efficiency** and recovery rates
- **Damage mitigation** and survival sustainability
- **Downed state resilience** and recovery

This branch is ideal for players who prefer:
- Frontline combat roles
- Supporting teammates with sustained pressure
- Long engagements without needing to retreat
- Surviving overwhelming odds

## 📊 Key Conditioning Nodes Breakdown

### Tier 1: Foundation (0-15 points)

**Iron Constitution (5 ranks)**
- Increases maximum health by 3% per rank
- Total: 15% health increase at max rank
- **Priority**: Essential for all builds

**Stamina Reserve (5 ranks)**
- Increases maximum stamina by 10% per rank
- Total: 50% stamina increase at max rank
- **Best for**: Players who frequently sprint and dodge

**Quick Recovery (5 ranks)**
- Reduces stamina regeneration cooldown by 8% per rank
- Total: 40% faster stamina recovery at max rank
- **Critical for**: Combat-heavy playstyles

### Tier 2: Efficiency (15-36 points)

**Shield Efficiency (5 ranks)**
- Reduces shield delay by 12% per rank
- Increases shield recharge rate by 15% per rank
- **Must-have**: For any combat build

**Second Wind (3 ranks)**
- Grants 20% stamina restoration on kill
- Cooldown: 30 seconds
- **Excellent for**: Aggressive players

**Damage Dampener (5 ranks)**
- Reduces incoming damage by 3% per rank
- Total: 15% damage reduction at max rank
- **Game-changer**: For survivability

### Tier 3: Mastery (36-75 points)

**Fortress (1 rank, requires 50 Conditioning points)**
- While above 50% health, gain 25% damage resistance
- **Condition**: Lose effect when health drops below 50%
- **Power spike**: Massive defensive boost

**Tenacity (5 ranks)**
- Reduces downed state duration by 20% per rank
- Increases revival speed by 15% per rank
- **Team utility**: Faster recovery means back in action sooner

**Last Stand (3 ranks)**
- When downed, can still move slowly and use secondary weapon
- Duration: 10 seconds + 2 per rank
- **Game-saving**: Can still contribute while downed

## 🎯 Optimal Conditioning Builds

### Build 1: The Immovable Object (Tank)

**Points**: 60 Conditioning / 15 Mobility

**Core Nodes**:
- Iron Constitution (5/5)
- Stamina Reserve (5/5)
- Shield Efficiency (5/5)
- Damage Dampener (5/5)
- Fortress (1/1)
- Tenacity (5/5)

**Secondary**: Mobility (Marathon Runner 5/5, Sprinter 5/5, Adrenaline Rush 5/5)

**Playstyle**: Absorb damage for the team, hold positions, and never retreat

**Pros**:
- Extremely durable
- Constant frontline presence
- High shield uptime

**Cons**:
- Slow movement speed
- Vulnerable to kiting
- Low damage output

### Build 2: The Resilient Fighter (Balanced)

**Points**: 45 Conditioning / 30 Mobility

**Core Nodes**:
- Iron Constitution (5/5)
- Quick Recovery (5/5)
- Shield Efficiency (5/5)
- Second Wind (3/3)
- Damage Dampener (3/5)
- Tenacity (3/5)

**Secondary**: Mobility (Marathon Runner 5/5, Combat Rolls 5/5, Evasive 5/5)

**Playstyle**: Survive extended fights while maintaining some mobility

**Pros**:
- Good balance of survival and speed
- Self-sufficient
- Versatile

**Cons**:
- Not as tanky as pure Conditioning
- Not as fast as pure Mobility

### Build 3: The Support Tank (Team-oriented)

**Points**: 50 Conditioning / 25 Survival

**Core Nodes**:
- Iron Constitution (5/5)
- Shield Efficiency (5/5)
- Damage Dampener (5/5)
- Fortress (1/1)
- Tenacity (5/5)
- Last Stand (3/3)

**Secondary**: Survival (Looter 5/5, Packer 5/5, Team Player 5/5)

**Playstyle**: Protect teammates, control space, support objectives

## 💡 Pro Tips for Conditioning Players

### Early Game (Levels 1-25)

1. **Max Iron Constitution first** - HP is king early game
2. **Quick Recovery (3/5)** - Just enough for basic stamina regen
3. **Save points** - Don't overcommit yet

### Mid Game (Levels 26-50)

1. **Shield Efficiency (5/5)** - Essential for combat effectiveness
2. **Second Wind (3/3)** - Great for extended fights
3. **Start Damage Dampener** - Begin path to Fortress

### Late Game (Levels 51-75)

1. **Fortress** - Game-changing defensive node
2. **Tenacity (5/5)** - Critical for team play
3. **Fill remaining** - Complete missing nodes

### Positioning Tips

- **Lead the charge** - You have the durability to absorb first contact
- **Hold choke points** - Use your damage reduction to control space
- **Protect supports** - Stay close to Survival players for mutual benefit
- **Time Fortress** - Monitor your health to maintain the 50% threshold

## 🔧 Synergies with Other Branches

### Conditioning + Mobility

- **Best for**: Frontline harassers
- **Strategy**: Use durability to get close, speed to flank
- **Key nodes**: Combat Rolls, Second Wind, Adrenaline Rush

### Conditioning + Survival

- **Best for**: Team anchors, objective holders
- **Strategy**: Maximize utility while being unkillable
- **Key nodes**: Loot speed, revives, inventory space

## 📈 When to Choose Conditioning

Choose Conditioning if you:
- Play in a coordinated team
- Prefer frontline combat
- Want to be the anchor for your squad
- Enjoy strategic positioning over mechanical skill
- Play support roles that require staying alive

## ❌ When to Avoid Conditioning

Avoid pure Conditioning if you:
- Play solo frequently
- Prefer hit-and-run tactics
- Rely on positioning over durability
- Want high damage output
- Enjoy fast-paced gameplay

## 🎓 Advanced Techniques

### Fortress Management

- **Monitor health threshold**: Stay above 50% for maximum benefit
- **Time engagements**: Activate before pushing, retreat if dropping low
- **Combine with shields**: Use Fortress during shield recharge windows

### Stamina Management

- **Pre-fight preparation**: Ensure full stamina before engaging
- **Pacing**: Don't exhaust all stamina on approach
- **Regen timing**: Use cover for Quick Recovery ticks

### Team Play

- **Body blocking**: Use your durability to protect teammates
- **Objective holding**: Station yourself on critical objectives
- **Revive priority**: Use Tenacity to recover downed teammates quickly

## 🔄 Seasonal Meta Considerations

**Current Meta**: After Update 1.7.2, Conditioning has seen a resurgence due to:
- Increased ARC damage output
- Longer engagement distances
- More bunker/close-quarters combat
- Team composition importance

**Recommended Investment**: 45-60 points for most players

---

**Conclusion**: The Conditioning branch offers unparalleled survivability and team utility. While it may not be the most glamorous choice, it's often the most valuable. Master Conditioning, and you'll become the foundation your team can rely on.

> 💡 **Next Steps**: Check out our [Mobility Branch Guide](https://arcraiderskill.com/blog/mobility-mastery-guide.html) and [Survival Branch Guide](https://arcraiderskill.com/blog/survival-branch-complete-guide.html) to complete your skill tree knowledge!

# ARC Raiders Skill Tree FAQ | Points, Builds & Respec

**URL:** https://arcraiderskill.com/faq.html

Find answers about ARC Raiders skill points, Conditioning, Mobility and Survival branches, build planning, prerequisites, sharing builds, and respec options.

---

# Frequently Asked Questions

### How many skill points do I get?

You receive 75 skill points total - one per level from level 1 to level 75.

### What are the three skill branches?

Conditioning (tanking), Mobility (speed), and Survival (looting/crafting).

### Can I reset my skill points?

Yes, but respec options are limited in-game. Use our planner to test builds first.

Legal Document

# Privacy Policy

Last updated: March 2026  ·  ARC Raiders Skill Tree Builder

01 / Overview

## Introduction

Welcome to **ARC Raiders Skill Tree Builder** ("we", "our", or "us"). This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, and protect information when you visit **arcraiderskill.com**.

This is a fan-made, community tool and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the developers of ARC Raiders. By using this site, you agree to the practices described below.

02 / Data We Collect

## Information We Collect

We collect minimal data to operate and improve the site:

- **Usage data** — pages visited, time on site, and referral source, collected anonymously via Google Analytics.

- **Build data** — skill tree builds are encoded in URL hash fragments and stored only in your browser. We do not store builds on our servers.

- **Cookies** — we use essential and analytics cookies. No advertising or tracking cookies are used.

- **Contact information** — if you email us, we store your email address solely to reply to your inquiry.

We do not collect names, addresses, payment details, or any sensitive personal data.

03 / Analytics

## Google Analytics

We use Google Analytics (GA4) to understand how visitors use the site. Google Analytics collects anonymized data such as device type, browser, country, and pages visited. This data is processed by Google in accordance with their Privacy Policy.

You can opt out of Google Analytics tracking using the [Google Analytics Opt-out Browser Add-on](https://tools.google.com/dlpage/gaoptout) or by enabling "Do Not Track" in your browser settings.

04 / Third-Party Content

## Embedded Third-Party Content

Some pages embed YouTube videos. When you play an embedded video, YouTube may collect data about your interaction in accordance with [Google's Privacy Policy](https://policies.google.com/privacy). We use YouTube's privacy-enhanced mode where possible.

We do not sell, rent, or trade your data to any third parties for marketing purposes.

05 / Your Rights

## Your Rights & Choices

Depending on your location you may have rights to access, correct, or delete your personal data. Because we collect very little personal information, most requests can be handled by:

- Clearing your browser cookies and local storage to remove any site-stored data.

- Using your browser's private/incognito mode to browse without cookies.

- Contacting us at the email address below for any other requests.

06 / Data Security

## Security

All traffic to this site is served over HTTPS. We do not operate databases containing personal user accounts or passwords. Skill builds are stored only in URL parameters on your device.

07 / Changes

## Changes to This Policy

We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. Changes will be reflected with an updated "Last updated" date at the top of this page. Continued use of the site after changes constitutes acceptance of the revised policy.

### Questions or Concerns?

If you have any questions about this Privacy Policy or how your data is handled, please reach out — we're happy to help.

[✉ support@arcraiderskill.com](mailto:support@arcraiderskill.com)

# ARC Raiders Skill Tree Wiki | Builds & Mechanics

**URL:** https://arcraiderskill.com/wiki.html

Complete ARC Raiders Skill Tree Wiki: Master Conditioning, Mobility, and Survival branches. Learn optimal build paths, node strategies, and pro tips for.

---

# Wiki & Quick Reference

Branches, mechanics, and quick build guidance.

## Branches

- Conditioning Stamina, shield efficiency, survival sustain. Good for tanks/long fights.

- Mobility Movement speed, rolls, vaulting, fall mitigation. Best for PvP/flankers.

- Survival Loot speed, inventory, crafting, stealth. Suited for solo/looters.

## Core Mechanics

- Max points: 75 total (one per level).

- Prerequisites: unlock parent nodes before children.

- Category gates: some nodes need category points (e.g., 15 / 36).

- Ranks: most nodes have 1 or 5 ranks; respect max rank caps.

- Respec: use the planner to test builds before committing in-game.

## Quick Builds

### Solo Looter

- Survival 40–50 pts, light Mobility.

- Focus: loot speed, backpack capacity, stealth noise reduction.

### Team Tank

- Conditioning 40–50 pts, some Survival.

- Focus: stamina regen, shield penalties, downed survivability.

### PvP Flanker

- Mobility 45–55 pts, low Conditioning.

- Focus: sprint/roll stamina, climb/vault speed, fall damage reduction.

## How to Use the Builder

- Pan/Zoom: drag to pan, scroll to zoom (0.4x–2.5x).

- Allocate: click nodes to add/remove points; watch category totals.

- Share: use "Share Build" to copy a link with your allocation.

- AI Assist: ask the Gemini assistant for scenario-based builds.

## FAQ

- **Best first picks?** Early Mobility (Marathon Runner) then Survival looting.

- **Can I respec?** In-game options are limited; plan here first.

- **Do hash links index?** Sections are referenced, but primary canonical is the main URL.
